{{Short description|Topological complexity in mathematics}}
In the mathematical field of [[geometric topology]], the '''simplicial volume''' (also called '''Gromov norm''') is a measure of the topological complexity of a [[manifold]]. More generally, the '''simplicial norm''' measures the complexity of [[homology class]]es.

Given a [[closed manifold|closed]] and oriented manifold, one defines the simplicial norm by minimizing the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients over all singular chains homologous to a given cycle. The simplicial volume is the simplicial norm of the [[fundamental class]].<ref name="bp92">{{citation
 | last1 = Benedetti | first1 = Riccardo
 | last2 = Petronio | first2 = Carlo
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-58158-8
 | isbn = 3-540-55534-X

 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=iTbmytIqdpcC&pg=PA105
 | year = 1992}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Ratcliffe | first = John G.|doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-4013-4
 | edition = 2nd
 | isbn = 978-0387-33197-3
 | location = Berlin
 | mr = 2249478
 | page = 555
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Graduate Texts in Mathematics
 | title = Foundations of hyperbolic manifolds
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=JV9m8o-ok6YC&pg=PA555
 | volume = 149
 | year = 2006| s2cid = 123040867}}.</ref>

It is named after [[Mikhail Gromov (mathematician)|Mikhail Gromov]], who introduced it in 1982. With [[William Thurston]], he proved that the simplicial volume of a finite volume [[hyperbolic manifold]] is proportional to the [[hyperbolic volume]].<ref name="bp92"/>

The simplicial volume is equal to twice the [[Thurston norm]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gabai |first=David |date=January 1983 |title=Foliations and the topology of 3-manifolds |journal=Journal of Differential Geometry |volume=18 |issue=3 |pages=445–503 |doi=10.4310/jdg/1214437784 |issn=0022-040X |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Thurston also used the simplicial volume to prove that hyperbolic volume decreases under [[hyperbolic Dehn surgery]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Benedetti|Petronio|1992}}, pp. 196ff.</ref>
